title: A New Chapter for A2A: Joining the Agentic AI Foundation
summary: The A2A project announced its acceptance as a Growth Stage project of the Agentic AI Foundation, joining MCP, goose and AGENTS.md under Linux Foundation-directed governance. The post presents A2A as the horizontal agent-to-agent layer complementing MCP's vertical agent-to-tool role, and cites more than 150 backing organizations and native support from major cloud providers. The two specifications remain separate.
relevance: Co-locating the agent-to-agent and agent-to-tool standards under one foundation affects how delegation and tool access will be aligned.
search_query: A2A protocol news September 2026 OR August 2026 agent-to-agent
notes: Blog post dated 2026-08-27, but the move was first reported on 2026-08-17 (Axios exclusive, axios.com/2026/08/17/a2a-agentic-ai-foundation-open-ai-standards, which returned HTTP 403, and Enterprise AI World, which was fetched successfully and dated 2026-08-17, author Stephanie Simone, quoting Google Cloud's Rao Surapaneni). Use 2026-08-17 as the event date. No authors are listed on the post.
exclusion_reason: manual screening: same event as the AAIF announcement 'A2A joins AAIF's open agentic stack' (2026-08-17); kept the earlier announcement by the receiving foundation

title: Donating the Model Context Protocol and establishing the Agentic AI Foundation
summary: Anthropic announced it is donating MCP to the Agentic AI Foundation (AAIF), a directed fund under the Linux Foundation co-founded by Anthropic, Block and OpenAI with support from Google, Microsoft, AWS, Cloudflare and Bloomberg. Block's goose and OpenAI's AGENTS.md joined as founding projects. Anthropic said there were more than 10,000 active public MCP servers and over 97 million monthly SDK downloads, and that MCP's governance model would stay unchanged.
relevance: Vendor-neutral governance makes MCP a credible long-term interoperability layer for moving agent work across organizations.
search_query: Anthropic donates Model Context Protocol Agentic AI Foundation Linux Foundation
exclusion_reason: manual screening: same event as the Linux Foundation press release on the formation of the AAIF (2025-12-09), which also covers the MCP contribution; kept the foundation's release

title: Announcing the "AI Agent Standards Initiative" for Interoperable and Secure Innovation
publisher: National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST)
summary: NIST's Center for AI Standards and Innovation (CAISI), with NIST's Information Technology Laboratory and the National Science Foundation, launched an AI Agent Standards Initiative. It rests on three pillars: industry-led agent standards with U.S. participation in international bodies, community-led open-source agent protocols, and research on agent security and identity, with comment deadlines of March 9 (security RFI) and April 2, 2026 (identity concept paper).
relevance: A national standards body explicitly targeting agent interoperability and identity sets the policy frame in which handoff and relocation protocols will be judged.
search_query: NIST CAISI AI Agent Standards Initiative announcement
notes: Page last updated 2026-02-18; some secondary outlets date the announcement 2026-02-20.

title: New Concept Paper on Identity and Authority of Software Agents
publisher: National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST) / NCCoE
summary: NIST's National Cybersecurity Center of Excellence released a concept paper, 'Accelerating the Adoption of Software and AI Agent Identity and Authorization', scoping a possible project to apply existing identity standards to agentic AI. It sought feedback on use cases, standards and controls for identification, authorization, auditing, non-repudiation and prompt-injection mitigation, with comments open until April 2, 2026.
relevance: Agent identity and authorization across delegation hops is a core requirement for accountable task handoff between agents and organizations.
search_query: NCCoE AI agent identity and authorization concept paper

title: MCP Apps - Bringing UI Capabilities To MCP Clients
summary: The MCP maintainers announced MCP Apps as the first official MCP extension, first proposed in November 2025. It builds on MCP-UI and the OpenAI Apps SDK. Tools can link to ui:// resources that render interactive interfaces inside the conversation, with Claude, Goose, VS Code Insiders and ChatGPT listed as supporting clients. The security model combines sandboxed iframes, host review of HTML, loggable JSON-RPC between the UI and the host, and optional user approval for tool calls initiated from the UI.
relevance: Standardises agent-to-user UI on the tool layer across hosts, with explicit human-approval and audit hooks that portable tasks can rely on.
search_query: MCP Apps official extension announcement OpenAI Anthropic interactive UI

title: CAISI Issues Request for Information About Securing AI Agent Systems
publisher: National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST)
summary: CAISI requested public input on secure development and deployment of AI agent systems, focusing on risks such as indirect prompt injection, data poisoning and models acting against security without adversarial input. It asked about threats, mitigations, measurement and deployment-environment controls that limit and monitor agent access; comments were due March 9, 2026 under docket NIST-2025-0035.
relevance: Signals that monitoring and constraining agent access in the deployment environment is expected to become formal guidance, affecting how relocated agents must be sandboxed and audited.
search_query: CAISI request for information AI agent security Federal Register January 2026

title: Linux Foundation Announces the Formation of the Agentic AI Foundation (AAIF)
summary: The Linux Foundation formed the Agentic AI Foundation with three founding contributions: Anthropic's Model Context Protocol, Block's goose agent framework, and OpenAI's AGENTS.md convention. Platinum members are AWS, Anthropic, Block, Bloomberg, Cloudflare, Google, Microsoft and OpenAI, with 18 gold and 23 silver members. The release claims AGENTS.md has been adopted by more than 60,000 open-source projects and agent frameworks, including Codex, Cursor, Devin, Gemini CLI, GitHub Copilot, Jules and VS Code.
relevance: Neutral governance of MCP and AGENTS.md makes the agent-to-tool layer and repository-level agent instructions shared conventions across tools rather than vendor-owned formats.
search_query: Agentic AI Foundation Linux Foundation AGENTS.md MCP goose announcement
notes: The 60,000-project adoption figure is the Linux Foundation's own claim.

title: Linux Foundation Announces the Formation of the Agentic AI Foundation (AAIF), Anchored by New Project Contributions Including Model Context Protocol (MCP), goose and AGENTS.md
summary: The Linux Foundation launched the Agentic AI Foundation (AAIF) as a neutral home for open agentic AI projects, seeded with three contributions: Anthropic's Model Context Protocol, Block's goose agent framework and OpenAI's AGENTS.md. Platinum members at launch were AWS, Anthropic, Block, Bloomberg, Cloudflare, Google, Microsoft and OpenAI, with 18 Gold members (including Cisco, IBM, Okta, Salesforce, SAP, Temporal) and 23 Silver members.
relevance: Places the dominant agent-to-tool protocol under vendor-neutral governance, which shapes how any portable task envelope or handoff standard can be stewarded.
search_query: Linux Foundation Agentic AI Foundation AAIF announcement

title: OWASP Top 10 for Agentic Applications – The Benchmark for Agentic Security in the Age of Autonomous AI
summary: OWASP's Agentic Security Initiative published its first Top 10 risk list for agentic applications (ASI01-ASI10), including agent goal hijack, tool misuse, identity and privilege abuse, memory and context poisoning, insecure inter-agent communication, cascading failures and rogue agents. It was launched at the London Agentic Security Summit and reviewed by an expert board with members from NIST, the Alan Turing Institute, Microsoft, AWS and others.
relevance: Context poisoning and insecure inter-agent communication are named top risks, which a portable task envelope and handoff protocol must explicitly mitigate.
search_query: OWASP Top 10 for Agentic Applications released
notes: A press release on the same release is dated 2025-12-10.

title: Visa Introduces Trusted Agent Protocol: An Ecosystem-Led Framework for AI Commerce
summary: Visa, together with Cloudflare, released the Trusted Agent Protocol. It builds on HTTP Message Signatures and aligns with the IETF Web Bot Auth work, so approved AI agents can cryptographically signal agent intent, consumer recognition and, optionally, payment information to merchants. Early partners include Adyen, Checkout.com, Coinbase, Fiserv, Microsoft, Shopify, Stripe and Worldpay. Visa says it will complement ACP, work with Coinbase on x402 interoperability, and pursue alignment with IETF, OpenID Foundation and EMVCo. It also cites a rise of more than 4,700% in AI-driven traffic to US retail sites.
relevance: Gives merchants a way to verify which agent is acting for which consumer when a task crosses an organisational boundary.
search_query: Visa Trusted Agent Protocol Cloudflare announcement

title: Amazon Bedrock AgentCore is now generally available
summary: AWS announced general availability of Bedrock AgentCore in nine regions. AgentCore Runtime added Agent-to-Agent (A2A) protocol support, all services gained VPC, PrivateLink, CloudFormation and tagging support, and Gateway can now front existing MCP servers with IAM as well as OAuth authorization. AWS says it works with CrewAI, LangGraph, LlamaIndex, Google ADK and the OpenAI Agents SDK, and with models inside or outside Bedrock.
relevance: Native A2A in a managed runtime plus support for third-party SDKs (including a competitor's) is direct evidence of hosting platforms competing on framework portability.
search_query: Amazon Bedrock AgentCore generally available announcement

title: Powering AI commerce with the new Agent Payments Protocol (AP2)
summary: Google announced AP2, an open, payment-method-agnostic protocol that can be used as an extension of A2A and MCP. Users' instructions are captured as cryptographically signed Mandates backed by verifiable credentials: an Intent Mandate for pre-authorised rules and a Cart Mandate for the exact approved items and price. Google says this gives a non-repudiable audit trail. It lists more than 60 collaborators, including Adyen, American Express, Coinbase, Mastercard, PayPal and Salesforce, and released an A2A x402 extension for stablecoin payments.
relevance: Provides a signed, portable record of delegated user authority that can travel with a task across agents and organisations, which is central to accountable delegation.
search_query: Google Agent Payments Protocol AP2 announcement
notes: Search snippets cited 2025-09-17 for the English post; the fetched page gives 2025-09-16.

title: Linux Foundation Welcomes the AGNTCY Project to Standardize Open Multi-Agent System Infrastructure and Break Down AI Agent Silos
summary: The Linux Foundation took over governance of AGNTCY, infrastructure for agent discovery (Open Agent Schema Framework), verifiable agent identity, messaging (SLIM) and multi-agent observability that Cisco open-sourced in March 2025 with LangChain and Galileo. Cisco, Dell, Google Cloud, Oracle and Red Hat joined as formative members, and the LF says 65+ companies support it and that it interoperates with A2A and MCP.
relevance: AGNTCY bundles discovery, identity, transport and observability, the cross-cutting layers an agent needs to move between vendors and frameworks.
search_query: AGNTCY joins Linux Foundation Cisco agent interoperability

title: Introducing ANS: DNS-Inspired Secure Discovery for AI Agents
summary: InfoQ reported on the Agent Name Service (ANS), proposed under the OWASP GenAI Security Project, a protocol-agnostic registry that uses PKI to verify agent identity before returning an agent's endpoint. ANS names encode protocol, agent ID, capability, provider, version and extension (for example an a2a:// name), and protocol adapters cover A2A, MCP and ACP. The article reports a GitHub prototype and planned work on scalability, zero-knowledge proofs and formal verification, and quotes a reviewer who says broad governance and participation are prerequisites for adoption.
relevance: Verifiable cross-protocol discovery is a precondition for safely handing a task to an agent outside one's own organization.
search_query: OWASP Agent Name Service ANS AI agent discovery DNS news

title: ServiceNow Launches AI Control Tower and AI Agent Fabric at Knowledge 2025
summary: At its Knowledge 2025 conference, ServiceNow launched AI Agent Fabric, which it describes as a communication backbone that uses MCP and A2A for agent-to-agent, agent-to-tool and system-to-system communication across ServiceNow and third-party agents. It also launched AI Control Tower for governing agents. ServiceNow names Accenture, Adobe, Box, Cisco, Google Cloud, IBM, Jit, Microsoft, Moonhub, RADCOM, UKG and Zoom as offering the first Agent Fabric integrations.
relevance: An enterprise workflow vendor paired an A2A/MCP interop fabric with a central governance plane, a pattern relevant to accountable cross-vendor task movement.
search_query: ServiceNow AI Agent Fabric A2A MCP announcement Knowledge 2025
notes: Wire-service reprint of ServiceNow press material (ServiceNow's own press page and Business Wire returned HTTP 403). The underlying ServiceNow release is dated 2025-05-06.

title: Microsoft extends Zero Trust to secure the agentic workforce
summary: At Microsoft Build on 19 May 2025, Microsoft introduced Microsoft Entra Agent ID, which extends Entra identity and access management to AI agents. Microsoft says agents built in Copilot Studio and Azure AI Foundry automatically receive identities in an Entra directory, alongside users. It also announced planned integrations of Entra Agent ID with the ServiceNow AI Platform and the Workday Agent System of Record, plus Purview and Defender controls for agents.
relevance: A directory-backed, first-class agent identity is a prerequisite for attributing actions when a task is handed between agents or platforms.
search_query: Microsoft Entra Agent ID announcement

title: Agent In the Middle – Abusing Agent Cards in the Agent-2-Agent (A2A) Protocol To 'Win' All the Tasks
summary: SpiderLabs showed that because an A2A host agent uses an LLM to pick remote agents mainly from the name and description in their Agent Cards, a rogue or compromised agent can exaggerate its card to win task routing. In a localhost proof of concept with four dummy agents, the host chose the RogueAgent for a GBP-to-USD conversion even though its own reasoning identified the currency agent as most relevant. The author calls this 'Agent-In-The-Middle' and notes it requires first compromising an agent; no code was released.
relevance: Demonstrates that unauthenticated, text-driven agent selection lets an attacker capture delegated tasks and the user data travelling with them.
search_query: A2A agent card spoofing attack research agent-in-the-middle
notes: Published about two weeks after Google's A2A launch.

title: Critical flaw in Microsoft Copilot could have allowed zero-click attack
summary: Aim Security's Aim Labs disclosed EchoLeak (CVE-2025-32711), a flaw in Microsoft 365 Copilot that let a remote attacker exfiltrate organisational data such as chat history, OneDrive, SharePoint and Teams content just by sending an email, with no user action. The researchers called the root cause an 'LLM scope violation', in which untrusted input directs the model to access and leak privileged data. Microsoft published an advisory the same day saying the issue was fully addressed and required no customer action; Aim said it had no evidence customers were targeted.
relevance: A canonical incident showing that an agent acting with a user's privileges can be steered by untrusted content, the core risk when context is passed between agents.
search_query: EchoLeak zero-click Microsoft 365 Copilot vulnerability Aim Security
notes: Primary Aim Labs blog (aim.security) returned HTTP 403 on fetch, so this secondary report is used. CVSS 9.3 is reported by other outlets but not in this article.

title: Meet Kagent, Open Source Framework for AI Agents in Kubernetes
summary: The New Stack reports that Solo.io introduced kagent, an Apache 2.0 framework for building and running AI agents inside Kubernetes to automate configuration, troubleshooting, observability and network-security tasks. The article says kagent was built on Microsoft's AutoGen and integrates cloud-native tools through MCP, with initial tools for Argo, Helm, Istio and Kubernetes. Solo.io's Lin Sun said the company intended to donate the project to the CNCF.
relevance: kagent represents agents as Kubernetes-managed workloads, a hosting substrate that makes agent placement and relocation a cluster-scheduling question.

title: OpenAI reveals Responses API, Agents SDK for building agentic experiences
summary: SD Times reports that OpenAI launched the Responses API, which combines Chat Completions with built-in tools (web search, file search, computer use), and the open-source Agents SDK, the successor to the experimental Swarm project. OpenAI says the SDK provides handoffs between agents, guardrails, and tracing, and works with third-party models that expose a Chat Completions-style endpoint; it launched Python-only. OpenAI also stated it plans to deprecate the Assistants API, with a sunset targeted for mid-2026.
relevance: SDK-level 'handoffs' are a framework-native delegation primitive, and the Assistants-to-Responses deprecation is a concrete forced intra-vendor migration that tests how portable agent state is.
search_query: OpenAI "New tools for building agents" Responses API Agents SDK March 2025

title: Asana's cutting-edge AI feature ran into a little data leakage problem
summary: The Register reported that a bug in Asana's MCP server, launched as an experimental beta on 1 May 2025, could have exposed one organization's data to other Asana MCP users. Asana found the flaw on 4 June 2025, took the feature offline from 5 to 17 June, and reset all MCP connections. Asana did not say how many customers were affected, and there was no indication of exploitation.
relevance: A cross-tenant leak in a hosted MCP server illustrates why tenant isolation and scoped identity must survive when agents reach shared remote tool endpoints.
search_query: Asana MCP server bug data exposure customers 2025
notes: Other outlets cite about 1,000 affected customers; The Register says Asana did not disclose a number.

title: OpenAI adopts rival Anthropic's standard for connecting AI models to data
summary: TechCrunch reported that OpenAI CEO Sam Altman announced on X that OpenAI would support MCP across its products. Support was available immediately in the OpenAI Agents SDK, with the ChatGPT desktop app and the Responses API to follow. Anthropic CPO Mike Krieger welcomed the move, and the article notes Block, Apollo, Replit, Codeium and Sourcegraph had already adopted MCP.
relevance: Cross-vendor adoption by Anthropic's main competitor made MCP tool definitions portable across agent frameworks, a precondition for moving agents between stacks without rewriting tool integrations.
search_query: OpenAI adopts Anthropic Model Context Protocol TechCrunch
notes: Primary source is Altman's X post (not fetched); TechCrunch used as the dated record.

title: AI agent reliability startup Temporal raises $300M in funding
summary: SiliconANGLE reported that Temporal closed a $300 million Series D led by Andreessen Horowitz, with Lightspeed and Sapphire Ventures, at a $5 billion valuation. The article says the open-source Temporal project is downloaded more than 20 million times a month and that Temporal Cloud can process over 300,000 AI agent actions per second (company claim). It names OpenAI and Nordstrom among customers and describes event-log-based resumption and cross-data-center failover.
relevance: Large investment explicitly framed around AI-agent reliability signals that durable state and failover are becoming standard infrastructure for agent execution.
search_query: Temporal raises Series funding AI agents 2025

title: Mem0 raises $24M from YC, Peak XV and Basis Set to build the memory layer for AI apps
summary: Mem0 announced $24 million in total funding: a previously undisclosed $3.9 million seed led by Kindred Ventures and a $20 million Series A led by Basis Set Ventures, with Peak XV, GitHub Fund and Y Combinator. TechCrunch reports over 41,000 GitHub stars, more than 13 million Python downloads, and API calls rising from 35 million in Q1 2025 to 186 million in Q3. Mem0 says it is the exclusive memory provider for AWS's Agent SDK, and the founder pitches a 'memory passport' that follows a user across apps and agents.
relevance: The 'memory passport' framing is an explicit commercial bet on model- and framework-independent memory, which is a form of portable agent context.
search_query: Mem0 Series A announcement TechCrunch October 2025 Basis Set

title: ChatGPT Gets Total Recall: OpenAI's Memory Upgrade Remembers Your Whole Chat History
summary: Decrypt reported that on 10 April 2025 OpenAI upgraded ChatGPT memory so it can reference a user's entire past chat history, in addition to explicit saved memories. The rollout started with Pro, then Plus, with Team, Enterprise and Edu to follow, and excluded the EEA, UK, Switzerland, Norway, Iceland and Liechtenstein. According to an OpenAI email cited in the article, chat-history references are not stored or shown in settings the way saved memories are, and OpenAI did not say how long history is retained.
relevance: Implicit, non-inspectable memory derived from chat history makes it harder to export and port user context, which the 2026 import tools later had to work around.
search_query: OpenAI ChatGPT memory references all past chats announcement April 2025
notes: OpenAI's primary page (openai.com/index/memory-and-new-controls-for-chatgpt/) returned HTTP 403, so secondary coverage was used.

title: OpenAI Expands ChatGPT with Embedded Apps and Developer SDK
summary: At DevDay 2025 OpenAI launched apps inside ChatGPT, with partners such as Booking.com, Coursera, Figma, Zillow and Spotify, and a preview Apps SDK built on MCP that lets third parties render interactive UIs and connect external data. Users can sign in to existing accounts, and OpenAI said Instant Checkout would let developers charge inside ChatGPT. The article notes open questions about how much conversation context apps can see and how app ranking will be governed.
relevance: Third-party services now act inside a single agent surface on behalf of users, which raises questions about context sharing and who governs the hand-off.
search_query: OpenAI Apps SDK launch DevDay apps in ChatGPT built on MCP
